> [!reminder] How this scene works
> This is the end of the night. Read one ending, the one that fits what happened. Each ending runs in the same order:
> 1. **The resolution.** What happened to the two hundred Shrewish and to Brackenmouth. Read it aloud.
> 2. **Nib.** One read-aloud for her secret told, one for it kept. Read the one that fits.
> 3. **The last word.** Kettle's line, then the closing read-aloud that ends the session.
> Tell the table the night is over when you finish. Then hand out anything owed: a Fell who has not had their Treasure Phase from the last fight takes it now.

> [!choice] Which ending
> - **The Fell sealed the shaft.** Read The Stone Holds.
> - **The shaft was held until the last raft, or never sealed, and nobody was left on the quay.** Read Emptied.
> - **The shaft was not sealed, and somebody was left on the quay.** Read The Last Raft. That happens if the loading at the river door never got running, or if Furze's food took a raft's room and nobody held the shaft until the end.
> - **Every Fell fell in the shaft.** Read Defeat.

## The Stone Holds

Everyone lives, and Brackenmouth stands. The root is walled off under the warren for good. If rafts went downriver in the night, they come back by noon.

> [!readaloud] Resolution: The stone holds
> By noon every Shrewish who left in the night is back, the rafts hauled up the river on long ropes, and the families are carrying their bundles back in through the river arch. Somebody has started cooking. Somebody else has started arguing about whose goat was in the bread room. The long ridge down the middle of the great hall floor is already being called Nib's Hump, and children are running along the top of it. Two hundred Shrewish are under stone again, and the stone held.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was told
> Nib stands on her bucket in the middle of the hall and tells them all, plainly, what she did. Nobody shouts. When she's finished, an old Shrewish at the back says, "Well, you'd better go and look under everybody else's, then," and Nib says, "Yes," and that's the end of it. She's gone downriver by evening with a pick and a lamp.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was kept
> Nib goes from family to family all morning, checking floors with her ear to the stone. Nobody asks her why. When she passes you, she touches the circle on her apron buckle and keeps walking.

> [!readaloud] The last word
> Kettle climbs up your arm to your shoulder, sits down and folds her paws. "Grandad says you can stay as long as you like," she says. "He says you can have a jar. Not the plums."

> [!readaloud] Closing: The end of the night
> Under the floor, behind a wall of stone you set with your own hands, a root as big as a house has stopped growing. Above it, a warren full of small people is asleep. You woke up last night under a pile of barley with no idea who you were. Brackenmouth knows exactly who you are.

## Emptied

Everyone lives, and Brackenmouth is lost. The Shrewish go downriver to Quillbark Hold with what they carried.

> [!readaloud] Resolution: Emptied
> The last raft swings out into the current with you on it. Behind you, through the river arch, the great hall fills with soft grey wood from the floor up, until the lamps on the pillars go out one by one. Two hundred Shrewish float down the Sallowrun in the dawn with what they could carry, toward Quillbark Hold. On every raft somebody is counting heads. Every count comes out right.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was told
> Nib sits at the back of the last raft and tells it to everybody in earshot, and then to the next raft over, shouting across the water. By the time Quillbark's quills show over the trees, all two hundred know. Nobody says anything to her. Somebody passes her a moss cake.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was kept
> Nib sits at the back of the last raft and watches Brackenmouth go out of sight. When it's gone, she takes a pencil from behind her ear and starts drawing on the raft's planks. She is drawing a warren, a new one, all stone, with a wall across the bottom of every shaft.

> [!readaloud] The last word
> Kettle is asleep in the coil of rope, and wakes up when the raft bumps. She looks back up the river, and then up at you. "We can build another one," she says. "Can't we? You're very strong."

> [!readaloud] Closing: The end of the night
> The river carries you on, slow and brown, between trees so tall you can't see their tops. Ahead, the quills of Quillbark Hold catch the first sun. Behind you, a warren is gone, and every one of the people who lived in it is on these rafts. The Shrewish around you have already started arguing about where the new one should go.

## The Last Raft

Most of them live. Brackenmouth is lost, and some Shrewish were left on the quay.

> [!reminder] Who was left
> Work out the number by the rule in The rafts in the overview: eighty if the loading never got running, twenty more if Furze's food rode without room. Name them by family before you read. The last twenty are Furze's neighbors from the bottom end.
> The Fell's raft is full to the rail. A Fell may give up their place and stay on the quay with the ones left behind. Let them. That Fell is with them when the table's next adventure begins: Brackenmouth, a week later, and the root in the hall.

> [!readaloud] Resolution: The last raft
> The last raft goes out full, and the quay is not empty behind it. You can see them from the water as the current takes you: families standing at the top of the steps with their bundles at their feet, watching you go. Behind them the grey is coming out of the river arch. Dobb counts the rafts out loud, gets to the end, and counts them again. The number doesn't change.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was told
> Nib tells the whole raft what she did. Halfway through she can't finish, and Dobb finishes it for her.

> [!readaloud] Nib, if her secret was kept
> Nib doesn't say anything all the way to Quillbark. She doesn't take her eyes off the river behind you.

> [!readaloud] The last word
> Kettle is sitting in your lap, very still. "I counted them too," she says. "Will you go back for them? You could. You're very strong."

> [!readaloud] Closing: The end of the night
> Quillbark Hold opens its gates to the rafts, and its people come down to the water with blankets and bread. Somebody is already writing names on a board by the gate, the ones who made it and the ones who didn't. You know some of the names on the second list now. You know which way the river runs back.

## Defeat

Every Fell fell at the bottom of the shaft. Nib dragged them out. Everyone on the rafts lives, and Brackenmouth is lost.

> [!reminder] Before you read
> Every Fell who fell went down into Pandemonium. Run [[Running Pandemonium]] as written for each of them first. A Fell who comes back wakes on the raft, and Nib's rope is how their body got there. Then work out who was left on the quay by the rule in The rafts in the overview, and name them in the closing. On this ending Nib tells her secret herself.

> [!readaloud] Resolution: Defeat
> You come to on a raft, on your back, looking up at a grey sky between enormous trees. The river is rocking you. You're soaked through and your whole body hurts. Nib is at the back of the raft bailing water with a bucket, and Dobb is poling, counting under his breath. Behind you, far up the river, grey dust is rising from the bank where Brackenmouth was.

> [!dialogue] Nib Sorrelgate
> *When the Fell ask how they got out:* "I went down and dragged you up the shaft one at a time on the rope, that's how. You're all very heavy. And it's my fault you were down there at all. I'll be telling everybody that when we get to Quillbark. All of it."

> [!readaloud] The last word
> Kettle crawls out of a pocket in somebody's coat. "You did very well," she says firmly. "Mostly."

> [!readaloud] Closing: The end of the night
> The rafts drift on toward Quillbark Hold. Every Shrewish who made it onto one is on the river with you. Anyone who didn't is back there with the root, and Dobb says their names under his breath between counts. Nib bails, and the trees go by.
